short_definition: A electronic device that uses optical cameras, radar sensors, or photometric imagery to measure ball flight and club performance metrics at impact.
money_page_anchor: our complete guide to the best launch monitors in Canada
canadian_context_note: In Canada, buying through authorized Canadian dealers ensures valid warranty coverage and avoids unexpected import duties at the border.

short_definition: Smash factor is the mathematical ratio of ball speed divided by club head speed, quantifying the energy transfer efficiency from club to ball at impact.
money_page_anchor: a launch monitor that tracks smash factor accurately
canadian_context_note: A PGA tour driver smash factor averages 1.48–1.50. During cold Canadian garage sessions, cold golf balls compress slightly less, temporarily reducing measured smash factor by 0.02–0.03.

short_definition: The velocity of the golf ball measured immediately after separation from the club face, measured in miles per hour (mph) or kilometers per hour (km/h).
money_page_anchor: launch monitors with high-speed ball velocity tracking
canadian_context_note: Ball speed is the single biggest factor in total carry distance. High-speed camera launch monitors capture ball speed instantly within 2 inches of movement.

short_definition: The vertical angle of the golf ball's initial flight path relative to the ground immediately upon leaving the club face.
money_page_anchor: optimizing launch angle on your home simulator
canadian_context_note: Achieving optimal launch angle is critical in indoor simulators where ceiling height constraints (minimum 9ft recommended in Canada) dictate vertical clearance.

short_definition: The amount of backspin rotation on the golf ball immediately after impact, measured in revolutions per minute (rpm).
money_page_anchor: photometric launch monitors with accurate spin measurement
canadian_context_note: Radar launch monitors require at least 8 to 10 feet of ball flight to measure spin accurately indoors, whereas photometric camera systems measure spin rate within 2 inches.

short_definition: The total airborne distance the golf ball travels from the impact spot to the point where it first strikes the turf.
canadian_context_note: Simulator software algorithms calculate carry distance based on ambient elevation and temperature. Setting your altitude correctly in Canadian cities like Calgary (3,400ft elevation) is vital.

short_definition: The linear velocity of the club head center immediately prior to impact with the golf ball, measured in mph.
money_page_anchor: launch monitors with direct club measurement
canadian_context_note: Unlocking club head speed data on high-end camera units allows Canadian golfers to conduct effective winter speed-training programs.

short_definition: A heavy-duty, tightly woven polyester or multi-layer mesh screen designed to safely stop full-speed golf ball impacts while displaying a clear projected image.
money_page_anchor: triple-layer low-noise impact screens in Canada
canadian_context_note: Triple-layer premium impact screens reduce ball bounce-back and muffle noise, essential for Canadian suburban home basements and attached garages.

name: Golf Simulator Enclosure
short_definition: A protective framework structure composed of metal piping, side baffle nets, ceiling blackout fabric, and an impact screen designed to contain shanked shots.
money_page_anchor: DIY and custom enclosure options available in Canada
canadian_context_note: Custom enclosure frames can be constructed using standard EMT conduit available at Canadian hardware retailers (Home Depot, Rona).

short_definition: A launch monitor detection technology that emits microwave signals to track the moving golf ball and club face over distance.
money_page_anchor: doppler radar vs photometric camera comparison
canadian_context_note: Radar units perform exceptionally well outdoors on Canadian driving ranges, but require generous room length (16+ ft) when installed indoors.

short_definition: A launch monitor technology that uses high-speed digital cameras to take multiple rapid flash photographs of the ball during the first few inches of flight.
canadian_context_note: Photometric camera systems are the preferred choice for Canadian garage and basement builds because they require zero ball-flight distance behind the net.

short_definition: A leading next-generation golf simulation software engine built on Unity, renowned for 4K ultra-realistic physics, community course creation, and open API compatibility.
money_page_anchor: GSPro software setup and licensing guide for Canadian golfers
canadian_context_note: GSPro features hundreds of Canadian courses rendered by community creators, including Banff Springs, St. George's, and Glen Abbey.

short_definition: An industry-standard golf simulation software platform developed by TruGolf, offering cross-platform play, multiplayer leagues, and extensive course libraries.
money_page_anchor: E6 Connect software bundles and launch monitor compatibility
canadian_context_note: E6 Connect comes bundled with many popular launch monitors sold in Canada, including SkyTrak+ and Full Swing KIT.
